title: Weil divisor and class groups for a commutative ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A height-one prime of $R$ is a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\neq(0)$ such that every prime $\mathfrak r\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ is $(0)$. The group of affine Weil divisors is $\operatorname{Div}(R)=\bigoplus_{\mathfrak q}\mathbf Z[\mathfrak q]$, the finitely supported functions from the height-one primes to $\mathbf Z$. For a height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ and $a\in R$ put $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak q}(a)=\operatorname{length}_{R_{\mathfrak q}}(R_{\mathfrak q}/aR_{\mathfrak q})$, computed in the localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] (an integer when finite, $0$ otherwise); when $R_{\mathfrak q}$ is a discrete valuation ring and $a\neq0$ this is the normalized valuation of $a$. The principal subgroup is generated by the divisors $d$ for which there are nonzero $a,b\in R$ with $d(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak q}(a)-\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak q}(b)$ for every $\mathfrak q$, and the affine Weil divisor class group $\operatorname{Cl}(R)$ is $\operatorname{Div}(R)$ modulo this subgroup.
